ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering (as amended) and Executive Regulation No. 222 of 2002; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its executive regulations; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; Commercial Registry Law No. 178 of 2021; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT regulations; Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) directives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national ID of each founding shareholder and each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/civil status authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization by Egyptian Embassy/Consulate followed by legalization of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Egypt. Hague Apostille is not recognized for Egypt because Egypt is not a contracting party to the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / certificate of incorporation of each corporate shareholder holding 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registrar of the foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization at Egyptian Embassy/Consulate, then Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization; additionally, Arabic certified translation must accompany the document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Founders' notarial declaration identifying UBOs and appointing the first director / general manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Egyptian Notary Public upon GAFI name clearance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before the Egyptian Notary Public; no apostille needed if executed in Egypt.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, authorized signatories and agents against the UN Security Council sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated sanctions list, Egyptian terrorist designation listing, and Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) databases. Positive hits require enhanced due diligence and mandatory filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU). CDD records must be retained for at least 5 years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Electronic Services Portal (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones - Investor Services / Company Establishment module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every Egyptian company must bear an Arabic commercial name. A Latin-script transliteration may be added for international use, but the Arabic name is authoritative for registration. The LLC legal suffix must be included in Arabic as 'Dhāt al-Masʼūlīyah al-Maḥdūdah' (Limited Liability Company). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name, trade mark, or distinctive commercial sign and must not violate public order or morals.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed once before expiration by submitting an extension application through GAFI's electronic portal and paying the renewal tariff. If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal to GAFI's Appeals and Complaints Committee within 15 working days of the rejection notice, using the official appeal form and attaching the rejection certificate. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may commence an administrative action before the Egyptian State Council (Conseil d'Etat) under the Administrative Procedure Law. As an alternative, the applicant may file a fresh name reservation with a modified name distinguishing it from the conflicting registered name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not accepted as the sole registered office for an airport runway asphalt paving contractor. GAFI and the Commercial Registry require a physical head office address evidenced by lease contract, utility bills and occupancy records. A serviced/virtual office may be used only as an auxiliary administrative address, but the licensed operational base and equipment site must be physically identifiable for inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High likelihood. GAFI and the local municipality, together with the Egyptian Civil Aviation Authority for runway works, perform mandatory pre-licensing site inspection and conduct unannounced site inspections during the performance of works; the estimated likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection is approximately 75% in the first operating year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2024, particularly Articles 129-143 governing Limited Liability Companies; investment-related provisions under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Documentation and Registration Directorate
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association (Aqd Ta'assys) and accompanying incorporation application submitted through GAFI One-Stop Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: LLC minimum paid-up capital under Law 159/1981 is EGP 50,000 (approximately USD 1,635), fully subscribed and deposited in an Egyptian licensed bank's escrow account; capital deposit certificate must be submitted with incorporation file, released only upon issuance of the registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) all issued shares as subscribed in the capital deposit certificate be accepted and credited to the Company's paid-up share capital; (2) the registered office be fixed at [address], Arab Republic of Egypt; (3) [name] be and is hereby appointed as Chairman/CEO, [name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [name] as Company Secretary, each authorized singly for ordinary operations and jointly for extraordinary matters; (4) such officers are empowered to open and operate bank accounts and to execute all contracts, filings, and license applications including civil aviation and environmental permits; and (5) the executive management be delegated to complete all statutory registrations with GAFI, tax and labor authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Trade name reservation and preliminary risk clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Economic Regions Department – One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit online name reservation via GAFI e-Services or OSS, proposing an Arabic and English trade name distinct from existing registrations. Obtain preliminary non-objection from Civil Aviation Authority for airport-paving activity if required by GAFI sector policy. Pay name reservation fee and receive reservation certificate valid for one year.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application
Passport copies of all founding shareholders or managers
Proposed Articles of Association draft
Pre-statutory approval from Civil Aviation Authority (if requested)
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is rejected for similarity, replace with a distinctive secondary name and resubmit; appeal refusal by filing a written objection with GAFI within 15 days and supply trademark search certificates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Association and manager appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Public Notary (Katib al-Adl) and GAFI-affiliated legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the founding meeting and sign the Articles of Association specifying shareholders, capital, shares, managers, registered office, duration and object clauses including 'airport runway asphalt paving and polymer-modified bitumen works'. Authenticate signatures of all founders before the competent public notary. Ensure the managers' declaration accepting appointment is appended and notarized.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association in Arabic
Identities of shareholders (passport copies or national IDs)
Name reservation certificate
Shareholder minutes of the founding general meeting
Consent to act as managers signed by each designated manager
Registered office preliminary lease agreement or title deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries any clause, revise the offending article and re-submit; if a founder refuses execution, amend the subscriber list and execute a restated Articles of Association.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit in an Egyptian licensed bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian central bank-licensed commercial banks with GAFI recognized escrow desks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate bank account in the name of the LLC under formation at an Egyptian bank, and transfer or deposit the full minimum paid-up capital (EGP 50,000) from shareholders abroad or in Egypt. Obtain a capital deposit certificate ('Certificate of Blocked Capital') stating that funds are irrevocably deposited pending registration. The bank will release funds only after the GAFI incorporation certificate is presented.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association and resolutions
Passport copies and proofs of address of shareholders transferring funds
Wire transfer or cash deposit slips
Bank account opening forms and KYC declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects non-resident deposits, present GAFI pre-approval and central bank permission under Law 194/2020; if capital inflow is delayed, use a GAFI approved foreign currency escrow and submit a bank undertaking letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation filing and registration with GAFI One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – One-Stop Shop (OSC) Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full statutory file to GAFI OSS in person or electronically through the GAFI e-portal. The OSS concurrently processes commercial registration (Commercial Registry No.) and tax registration (tax card) after incorporation certificate issuance. Pay official stamp fees and filing fees. The incorporation certificate constitutes the company's legal personality commencement date.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association (original + two certified copies)
Capital deposit certificate from the bank
Name reservation certificate
Registered office lease registration or ownership document
Passport copy and criminal record extract for each manager
Board resolution appointing officers and common seal specimen declaration
GAFI incorporation application form
Civil Aviation non-objection (if requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI requests clarifications or additional documents, respond within 15 working days; any rejection must be justified in writing and may be appealed to GAFI's Internal Grievance Committee within 30 days, or re-file after curing missing items.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation statutory registrations and company seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority, National Social Insurance Authority, Commercial Registry, and GAFI Labor Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the incorporation certificate, complete mandatory registrations: obtain the tax card and VAT registration; register managers and employees with the Social Insurance Authority; obtain labor office file; purchase approved company seal; and open operational corporate bank account to replace temporary account. For airport runway asphalt projects, initiate the industrial/civil aviation physical licensing in parallel.
required_dossiers: Incorporation certificate from GAFI
Commercial registration extract
Board resolution delegating signature and registration authorities
Copy of Articles of Association and tax card application form
Manager personal identifications and appointment letters
Certificate of capital deposit release or bank statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax card issuance is delayed, submit a provisional tax declaration and obtain a receipt; if social insurance complains about missing records, file corrected payroll data and pay incremental contributions with late fees.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA), Ministry of Trade and Industry, in coordination with the Egyptian Civil Aviation Authority (ECAA) for airport-adjacent asphalt paving operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Establishment Operation License (Rukhas Tashgheel Al-Mansha'a Al-Sina'i) under Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017, supplemented by a Civil Aviation Works Permits/Asphalt Plant Approval

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) required because the asphalt mixing and polymer-modified bitumen production emit particulate matter, VOCs, and potential wastewater pollution.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with Law 4/1994 as amended by Law 9/2009: wastewater to public sewer must have BOD ≤ 600 mg/L, COD ≤ 800 mg/L, TSS ≤ 800 mg/L, oil & grease ≤ 50 mg/L, pH 6-9.5; ambient air for PM10 ≤ 150 µg/m3, SO2 ≤ 125 µg/m3, VOC limits per EEAA technical guidelines; waste handling per hazardous waste rules and third-party disposal permits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Department fire safety certificate for asphalt plant, fuel storage, and drying drum; structural load inspection certificate for mixers and elevated silos from an accredited engineer; occupational safety and health clearance from the Ministry of Manpower; licences for on-site flammable material storage and hot-mix handling per the Egyptian Fire Protection Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), attached to the Ministry of Finance. Electronic services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing and e-receipt integration platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg; customs single window: NAFIZA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC (EG_LLC) must register with the ETA before commencement of activity or within 30 days of the first taxable supply. Steps: (1) notarize and Arabic-certify the LLC's constitutional documents and commercial register extract; (2) file the Tax Card application at the competent ETA office attaching the LLC contract, notarized power of attorney for the foreign manager, lease or works contract, and passports of signatories; (3) obtain the unified Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and VAT certificate within approximately 2-4 weeks; (4) integrate the taxpayer with the ETA e-invoicing/e-receipt platform and obtain the digital signature certificate; (5) complete NAFIZA customs registration for export operations. Non-resident contractors without a permanent establishment may appoint a resident tax representative for registration and compliance; VAT registration is mandatory within 30 days of exceeding the statutory turnover threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Egyptian law provides no check-the-box or pass-through election; an LLC is automatically a juridical person taxed at entity level under the Unified Tax Law (Law No. 30 of 2023), with a standard corporate income tax rate of 22.5%. No hybrid-mismatch fiscal-transparency election is available; controlled foreign company, transfer pricing, and anti-hybrid rules apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended by the Unified Tax Law (Law No. 30 of 2023)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual turnover of taxable goods and services, triggering mandatory VAT registration. Non-resident suppliers of services are subject to reverse-charge rules; SCZone free-zone projects may apply zone-specific VAT suspension or zero-rating instead of standard registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory near-real-time fiscal clearance: B2B e-invoices and B2C e-receipts must be generated in the ETA-prescribed XML/JSON schema, digitally signed with the taxpayer's ETA-issued certificate, and submitted via certified APIs to the ETA integration platform. The ETA validates fields and returns a QR-encoded clearance/acceptance code; invoices lacking clearance are non-compliant, and input VAT deduction is denied. Offline submission is tolerated only during declared ETA system outages.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies where (i) goods are physically exported from Egypt or delivered to free zones, evidenced by an electronic customs export declaration released through NAFIZA; (ii) services, including airport runway paving and polymer-modified asphalt works, are supplied to a non-resident principal and effectively consumed outside Egypt; or (iii) the supply qualifies under the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) free-zone regime. Construction services performed on-site within Egypt for a domestic airport operator are standard-rated at 14%; zero-rating is available only when the work is performed under an export-oriented contract with a non-resident principal, an international civil aviation contractor, or a qualifying SCZone project. The exporter must evidence receipt of payment in foreign currency through an Egyptian licensed bank and must repatriate proceeds within the applicable Central Bank of Egypt deadline; input VAT on exported supplies is refundable through the ETA's risk-based refund track.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration released through NAFIZA (Single Administrative Document)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exportation
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by an Egyptian licensed bank evidencing receipt of hard currency
Signed export contract, irrevocable letter of credit or civil aviation works order, and final commercial invoice
Certificate of Origin and any TIR/carnet documentation
Packing list, weight/tally certificate, and insurance certificate
ETA-cleared zero-rated e-invoice bearing the QR code and export VAT code
Contractor's completion and acceptance handover certificate for the runway paving works
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating and refund claims are subject to mandatory desk/field audit and ETA risk-scoring; incomplete export documentation within the statutory response period triggers reversal of the refund. Fraudulent zero-rating exposes the taxpayer to a fine of not less than 100% and not exceeding 300% of the evaded VAT plus imprisonment under VAT Law No. 67/2016 Article 37 and the Tax Procedures Law No. 206/2020, retrospective clawback of refunded VAT with monthly default interest, customs penalties, and suspension or cancellation of the taxpayer's e-invoicing clearance certificate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020, together with the relevant Egyptian banking, customs, investment, anti-money-laundering, and foreign-exchange regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian pound is generally convertible for bona fide current-account transactions through licensed banks, including documented imports, services, debt service, dividends, and other permitted commercial payments. Capital-account transactions, foreign direct investment movements, shareholder loans, intercompany funding, and repatriation of liquidation proceeds are subject to bank documentation, source-of-funds verification, investment and corporate records, tax clearance where applicable, and CBE or other regulatory requirements. There is no general prohibition on foreign ownership or dividend remittance by an Egyptian LLC, but practical delays may arise from foreign-currency liquidity, enhanced compliance reviews, incomplete customs or tax files, mismatches between contracts and invoices, sanctions screening, beneficial-owner concerns, or restrictions applicable to specific goods, counterparties, or jurisdictions. Dividends should be remitted from distributable profits supported by approved financial statements, shareholder resolutions, tax evidence, and proof of payment of applicable Egyptian taxes. Shareholder-loan repayments and capital reductions require evidence of the original inflow, the underlying agreement, corporate approvals, and bank acceptance. Payments must normally be executed through Egyptian licensed banks or other duly licensed payment institutions; offshore digital accounts do not substitute for an Egyptian banking channel for regulated local collections or FX conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Egypt does not generally impose a universal mandatory conversion ratio requiring every exporter to surrender a fixed percentage of export proceeds into Egyptian pounds. Export proceeds must nevertheless be handled through authorized banking channels and supported by export declarations, commercial invoices, shipping and customs records, contracts, and evidence of receipt. A single universal statutory repatriation deadline should not be assumed: applicable timing can depend on CBE instructions, customs and trade-finance rules, the exporter's banking arrangement, the commodity, destination, payment terms, and any approved extension or exception. The company should obtain a written transaction-specific position from its servicing bank before shipment and monitor outstanding export receivables against customs records. Foreign-currency retention, conversion, and use of proceeds are subject to bank controls, documentary consistency, AML review, and available CBE rules. Any mandatory conversion or repatriation requirement applicable to a particular export transaction must be confirmed against the current CBE and banking instructions in force on the transaction date.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for supplemental treasury tools and low for core Egyptian collections, FX conversion, payroll, or trade settlement. An offshore electronic-money institution or payment service provider generally cannot independently provide regulated Egyptian deposit-taking, local payment collection, Egyptian-pound conversion, domestic clearing, or trade-finance services unless it operates through an appropriately licensed Egyptian bank or payment provider and satisfies applicable CBE, AML, sanctions, tax, data, and foreign-exchange requirements. Offshore accounts may be used for permitted group treasury functions, but they should not receive Egyptian customer proceeds or fund regulated local activity without a documented Egyptian banking route. The LLC should maintain an Egyptian operational account and use the offshore provider only after bank and legal confirmation of the proposed flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is not invariably mandated by statute for every company account, but Egyptian banks commonly require in-person verification of authorized signatories, submission or inspection of original corporate documents, certified translations or legalization, specimen signatures, beneficial-owner identification, and a relationship-manager interview. Remote onboarding may be available on a bank-by-bank basis under CBE-approved electronic-KYC procedures, but it should not be presumed for a newly incorporated LLC, foreign-owned entity, high-value construction contractor, or account requiring foreign-currency and trade-finance services. At least one locally authorized signatory and an Egyptian registered address are normally operationally important. Foreign directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners should expect passport, address, tax-residency, source-of-wealth, and notarization or legalization requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder or beneficial owner is difficult to identify, uses a layered holding structure, or has inconsistent ownership information across corporate records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current commercial-register extract; constitutional documents; complete ownership chart to the ultimate natural persons; passports and proof of address for all relevant beneficial owners; shareholder register; director resolutions; tax-residency information; certified translations; notarization, legalization, or apostille where accepted; and a signed beneficial-ownership declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital inflow is received from an account that does not match the registered shareholder, subscribed capital, or stated investment purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank transfer confirmation and SWIFT message; shareholder funding agreement; subscription or capital-increase resolution; amended constitutional documents where applicable; GAFI or other investment filings where applicable; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; intercompany relationship chart; and written payment-purpose narrative matching the bank instruction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model involves airport infrastructure, public-sector contractors, government-linked entities, or politically exposed persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tender or contract documents; counterparty ownership and sanctions screening; beneficial-owner and PEP assessments; procurement approvals; anti-bribery and corruption policy; third-party due-diligence files; invoice and milestone schedule; payment-flow map; conflict-of-interest declarations; and evidence that commissions and agents are commercially justified and contractually documented.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or unusual cross-border payments lack a clear connection to runway paving, asphalt, plant, equipment, materials, engineering, or subcontracting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial contract; purchase order; invoice; bill of lading or transport documents; customs declarations; certificate of origin; technical specifications; delivery or acceptance certificate; subcontractor agreement; project budget; payment certificate; and reconciliation between the payment amount, construction milestone, and accounting records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-currency receipts, export proceeds, or remittances show repeated round amounts, rapid pass-through activity, unexplained third-country routing, or inconsistent transaction descriptions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling cash-flow forecast; customer and supplier ledger; contract register; invoice-to-bank reconciliation; explanation of treasury policy; intercompany settlement schedule; board-approved payment matrix; evidence of underlying goods or services; and written bank pre-clearance for exceptional routing or currency conversion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected account activity materially exceeds the submitted business plan or declared turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year financial model; awarded project contracts; tender pipeline; tax registrations; audited or management accounts; working-capital facility documents; project cash-flow schedule; expected monthly transaction volumes; currencies and countries matrix; and board-approved treasury and delegated-authority policies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Documents are issued in foreign languages, contain inconsistent legal names, or lack required certification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consistent legal-name schedule; certified Arabic or English translations as required by the bank; notarized and legalized or apostilled corporate documents; certificates of incumbency or good standing; powers of attorney; signatory specimen documents; and a document-control index linking each document to the relevant corporate record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Proposed counterparty, bank, vessel, insurer, or beneficial owner creates sanctions, export-control, or correspondent-bank screening exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-transaction screening results; full counterparty and beneficial-owner information; end-use and end-user statement; origin and destination analysis; product classification; shipping route; contractual sanctions representation; screening escalation record; and compliance approval before payment initiation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests for dividend, shareholder-loan, capital-reduction, or liquidation remittance are unsupported by distributable profits or original capital evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved financial statements; auditor report; shareholder resolution; tax filings and tax-payment evidence; retained-earnings computation; original capital-inflow records; loan agreement and repayment schedule where relevant; corporate approvals; liquidation or capital-reduction filings where applicable; and bank remittance application.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a direct SWIFT transfer from the foreign shareholder or clearly documented group treasury entity to the Egyptian LLC's foreign-currency capital or designated investment account at a CBE-licensed bank. The remittance instruction should identify the legal entity, shareholder or lender, purpose as subscribed capital, capital increase, or documented shareholder loan, and the relevant corporate resolution or agreement. Avoid third-party funding, personal accounts, cash deposits, unexplained netting, and multi-hop routing. Before receipt, provide the bank with the commercial registration, constitutional documents, ownership chart, shareholder resolution, subscription or loan agreement, source-of-funds evidence, and any required GAFI, investment, or corporate filing. After receipt, obtain the bank credit advice and SWIFT evidence, reconcile the amount to the corporate records, and complete any capital-registration or amendment filings. Conversion into Egyptian pounds should occur only for identified local expenditure and through the licensed bank at the applicable bank-confirmed rate. Repatriation of unused capital, loan principal, or dividends should use the same documented bank relationship and should not be characterized as a different purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For imported asphalt, bitumen, polymers, machinery, aircraft-runway equipment, spare parts, and engineering inputs, use the Egyptian LLC's bank account and provide the underlying purchase contract, pro forma or commercial invoice, customs and import documentation, product and end-use information, shipping documents, insurance evidence, and supplier and beneficial-owner details. A documentary commercial letter of credit issued or confirmed through a CBE-licensed bank is preferred for high-value or unfamiliar suppliers; the bank may transmit authenticated SWIFT messages and release payment against compliant documents. SWIFT MT103 may be used for open-account, advance, milestone, or documentary payments where the bank accepts the risk and the underlying transaction is documented. Documentary collection, bank guarantee, and standby structures may be available subject to bank approval and applicable trade rules. Payment descriptions, invoice values, customs declarations, tax records, and accounting entries must match. Do not split payments to evade review, route through unrelated offshore accounts, or use personal accounts. For outbound subcontractor, consultant, insurance, freight, and project payments, retain the contract, invoice, tax treatment, withholding analysis, service-delivery evidence, and any required tax certificates before remittance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a CBE-licensed bank, subject to an identifiable underlying exposure, approved limits, documented maturity, currency, amount, and settlement source.

Non-deliverable forwards, where offered by a properly licensed bank and permitted under current CBE and bank policies; availability, eligible currencies, settlement mechanics, and customer classification must be confirmed before execution.

Foreign-currency swaps or cross-currency swaps arranged with a licensed bank for documented funding, import, export, or receivable exposure; the company should maintain board approval, confirmations, valuation records, collateral terms, and exposure reconciliations.
Foreign-currency options or collars, if offered and approved by the servicing bank, subject to suitability, disclosure, accounting, and underlying-exposure requirements.

Natural hedging by matching foreign-currency project receipts with documented foreign-currency imports, debt service, and subcontractor obligations, without creating unlicensed payment-netting or deposit-taking activity.

The LLC should prohibit speculative derivatives, unsupported notional volumes, back-to-back arrangements with unlicensed intermediaries, and hedge settlements that lack a traceable underlying commercial exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 45) covering global taxable profits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Large Taxpayer Center once registration thresholds are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the taxable year-end (30 April for calendar-year taxpayers); extended to 5 months where audited accounts are obligatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing penalty equal to 2% of the outstanding tax per month (minimum EGP 200 per month, aggregate cap of 36% of tax due); automatic default assessment by the ETA; statutory interest at the Central Bank lending rate plus 2 percentage points; enforced bank-account attachment and eventual administrative registration suspension.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation and Ownership-Chain Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - National UBO Electronic Database
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, aligned with the Commercial Registry renewal cycle (January), plus a 30-day deadline for filing any intermediate share transfer or capital-structure change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and processing blocks under Egypt's Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 8 of 2008; GAFI refusal to notarize or certify LLC share transfers; shareholder distributions and general-assembly resolutions stayed until the UBO file is current; criminal exposure for material concealment of beneficial ownership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry Annual Renewal and Financial Data Amendment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office (GAFI one-stop shop for investment-licensed entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During January of each calendar year under Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; retroactive filing rejected after the month-end addendum
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal surcharge of approximately EGP 500 per month in addition to the annual fee; suspension of the commercial file; inability to execute contracts, clear customs, or operate bank letters of credit; prolonged delinquency leads to administrative deletion of the commercial registration record.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal completed on or before 31 December, effective for the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal blocks participation in public-sector and civil-aviation project tenders, customs clearances, and governmental vendor registries; renewal is refused until all ETA returns and dues are settled; reactivation requires a tax-clearing application and disclosure of books.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Construction Contracting Classification Certificate Renewal (roads and airport runway paving category)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Federation for Construction and Building Contractors (EFCBC) / Ministry of Housing, Utilities and Urban Communities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted each January with audited financial statements, technical staffing records, and completed project certificates for the prior fiscal year; certificate valid through 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or downgrade of the classification degree; mandatory exclusion from public-works and airport runway paving tender lists; reclassification audit and potential revocation of the entity's capacity to perform ISIC 4210 asphalt paving contracts in Egypt.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Civil Aviation Works Provider License Renewal (airside runway construction authorization)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Civil Aviation Authority (ECAA) - Ministry of Civil Aviation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the principal license anniversary date under Civil Aviation Law No. 151 of 1981; application accompanied by renewed tax card, classification certificate, and safety/quality compliance file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate suspension of airside permits and airport security passes; revocation of runway-paving authorization; administrative fines for unstayed works; continuation of works without a valid license constitutes an irregular aviation-side operation subject to ECAA enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory annual independent audit for all Egyptian LLCs irrespective of revenue level (at least one certified auditor under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; a second auditor is required where subscribed capital exceeds the statutory threshold, effectively EGP 1,000,000 as updated by executive interpretations). Any public-works or runway-paving contractor holding an EFCBC classification degree must always present audited financial statements for annual classification renewal and to the Egyptian Tax Authority.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued by the Ministry of Finance and substantially converged with IFRS; listed, regulated, or consolidated groups adopt full IFRS with EAS reconciliation; taxable income derives from net income as presented in the audited EAS financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Egyptian LLC must register and annually reconfirm its natural-person ultimate beneficial owners through GAFI's national UBO electronic database. The annual confirmation restates ownership percentages, any transfers executed during the year, and current identification documents. LLC share transfers are valid against third parties only after notarization, amendment of the share ledger, and GAFI UBO database update within 30 days; the annual UBO confirmation is synchronized with the January Commercial Registry renewal cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 1,500 per annum for a Cairo/Giza-based registered office or corporate secretarial agent, including domestic regulatory representation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 7,000 per annum for the mandatory audited financial statements of a medium-sized construction and paving LLC, increasing if IFRS/consolidation or ETA Large Taxpayer Center reporting applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% standard corporate income tax rate for tax periods beginning on or after 1 January 2024 under Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended by the 2023 budget amendment (prior rate: 20%). The special 40.55% regime for oil, gas, and Suez Canal activities does not apply to ISIC 4210 airport runway asphalt paving.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Egypt does not grant blanket tax holidays. Applicable incentives: (i) Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 - eligible projects in GAFI-approved governorates and development zones may deduct up to 50% of investment costs from taxable income; (ii) SCZONE free-zone registered projects are CIT-exempt on qualifying proceeds but must pay an annual duty of up to 1% of gross product value; (iii) standard ETA tax-depreciation schedules govern fixed-asset deductions; (iv) loss carryforward is limited to 5 years. No special CIT holiday is available for a mainland asphalt-paving LLC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 41 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return for juridical persons) filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) unified electronic services portal (eta.gov.eg) and the mandatory e-invoicing gateway. The return must attach the audited financial statements, tax-depreciation schedule, and, where thresholds are met, the transfer pricing Local File disclosure.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return plus quarterly provisional CIT filings. Quarterly advance payments equal to 25% of the prior-year assessed tax are due in each quarter and are credited against the final annual liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final Form 41 must be filed within 4 months after the close of the tax year (Law No. 91 of 2005). A 31 December year-end filer must file by 30 April; a 30 June government-aligned year-end filer must file by 31 October. Quarterly provisional returns and advance payments are due within one month after each quarter-end. Extensions are not routinely granted and late filings trigger automatic penalty accrual.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calendar or fiscal-year period covered by the return, stated as DD/MM/YYYY to DD/MM/YYYY consistent with the audited books.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian permanent establishment (PE) must file for the same tax period as its Egyptian statutory books; a foreign contractor cannot file using the parent's home-country fiscal year if that year differs from the PE's Egyptian accounting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, commercial register number, tax card number, share capital, shareholder list, and GAFI/SCZONE license numbers as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Egyptian PE registration number, the foreign parent's jurisdiction of residence, and the foreign tax identification number; attach the POA of the Egyptian tax representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ISIC 4210 / NAICS 237310: airport runway construction and polymer-modified bitumen asphalt paving; specify civil aviation authority project reference and license approval numbers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the PE scope precisely, including the airport-site contract and the construction-PE exposure arising from presence on the Egyptian site exceeding the treaty's minimum threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All revenues from paving contracts, including mobilization fees, variation orders, and reimbursable costs; foreign-currency amounts converted to EGP at the Central Bank of Egypt exchange rate on revenue recognition date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize only Egypt-source revenue attributable to the Egyptian site; back-to-back invoicing through an offshore intermediary must be eliminated unless fully supported by substance and transfer pricing analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bitumen, polymer modifiers, aggregates, subcontractor costs, labor, fuel, and equipment running costs, evidenced by mandatory e-invoiced supplier documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recharges from a foreign head office are deductible only where actually incurred for the Egyptian PE and priced at arm's length; unsupported allocated overhead is an add-back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rent, salaries, insurance, engineering supervision, and administrative overhead directly attributable to the contracting activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office management fees are deductible only to the extent a genuine service is rendered, documentation is retained, and the fee does not represent a disguised dividend or profit distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisions and general reserves (unless expressly allowed), statutory fines, penalties, donations above limits, and personal expenses of owners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any home-office royalty or notional interest charge where the foreign licensor lacks economic substance and where the charge fails the ETA beneficial-ownership and genuine-arrangement tests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation computed on ETA category schedules under Law No. 91 of 2005 based on historical asset cost; include asphalt plants, paving machinery, and vehicles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only assets physically used by the Egyptian PE are depreciable; assets held on the foreign parent's books cannot be depreciated in the Egyptian return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct tax losses carried forward from prior periods, subject to the 5-year limitation and the requirement that the same activity and books continue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE losses are ring-fenced to the Egyptian PE income and cannot be offset against foreign head-office profits, nor surrendered to group affiliates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net adjusted taxable income after add-backs, statutory depreciation, and loss relief; the result must reconcile to the audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are taxed only on Egypt-source income attributable to the PE; all runway contract proceeds derived from Egyptian civil aviation work are Egypt-source and fully taxable at 22.5%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Tax Rate and Tax Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 22.5% standard CIT rate to adjusted taxable income; compute tax due before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs are taxed at the same 22.5% rate; no separate branch-profits tax applies, and the 10% dividend withholding tax only attaches when profits are actually distributed by the Egyptian LLC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct quarterly advance CIT instalments and any Egyptian withholding tax borne on the taxpayer's income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim Egyptian WHT credits actually borne by the PE and, where a DTA applies, pursue treaty-reduced withholding at source before relying on refund procedures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 13 - Final Tax Payable or Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final liability after credits; overpayments are refundable through ETA procedures subject to audit clearance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any over-withheld treaty tax must be claimed in writing from the ETA within the statutory limitation period (generally 5 years) with TRC, apostillisation, and full wire documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 41: administrative fine of EGP 500 to 5,000 per return, with automatic escalation for large taxpayers, plus a monetary surcharge of 2% per month on the unpaid tax, accruing daily from the day after the statutory deadline until full settlement. Late-payment surcharges compound monthly and are not waivable in cases of negligence. Additional fines arise for e-invoice non-compliance under the VAT regime (Law No. 67 of 2016) and for failure to submit transfer pricing documentation on demand (up to EGP 100,000). The ETA may also withhold the tax clearance certificate required for renewal of civil aviation and public-works tenders.
